query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of 5-10 vol% Cu into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy via mechanical alloying and subsequent spark plasma sintering will improve the compressive strength and thermal conductivity of the alloy without sacrificing its caloric response.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of 5-10 vol% Cu into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy via mechanical alloying and subsequent spark plasma sintering
generation.conditions: Applied-field: 0-5 T, pressure-field: 0-100 MPa, temperature: 250-350 K, loading regime: compressive loading at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.structural_mediator: Cu-rich phase at grain boundaries and triple junctions
generation.mechanism: The Cu-rich phase acts as a ductile phase, enhancing the toughness and integrity of the alloy, while the high-entropy alloy matrix maintains its caloric response. The high thermal conductivity of Cu also facilitates heat transport
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive strength (> 200 MPa) and thermal conductivity (> 5 W/mK) without sacrificing caloric response, as compared to the baseline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy
generation.boundary: Applied-field: 0-5 T, pressure-field: 0-100 MPa, temperature: 250-350 K, loading regime: compressive loading at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The effect of Cu addition on the caloric response of the alloy is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the caloric response of the Cu-containing alloy and compare it to the baseline alloy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the caloric response of the Cu-containing alloy is significantly reduced compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
